status: MD/MM optimization is reopened under A2A. v18 repaired the stale 'mission closed / G1 next' state. v19 lands one correctness fix found during the optimization pass: Hardware::m_ucBatchEnabled now actually mirrors isFirmwareMidiReady(), so UC batch enable/disable transitions can be toggled both ways instead of repeatedly setting only the Microcontroller flag. v21 adds opt-in RT JIT attribution to the MM firmware test and confirms the big steady-state render spikes correlate with synchronous live DSP JIT compilation, not transport clamp/backpressure. v22/v23 add opt-in DSP JIT PC/reason tracing and reject the first naive static graph prewarm attempt. v23 evidence: repeated live JIT PCs are explained by multiple DSP SR-mode chains, not by repeated P-memory invalidation. v24 rejects the next hot-PC existing-chain prewarm prototype by measurement and reverts it. v25 classifies live JIT entries as mostly cold create(), not recreate(). v26 proves a cycle-counted interpreter primitive for future fallback/deferred work, but rejects a naive one-step RT interpreter fallback experiment by measurement and reverts that hook. v27 rejects the follow-up queued cold-create fallback prototype: even with a post-callback compile pump and fallback budgets of 128 or 1, the MM firmware test timed out and halted at INVALID PC ff0000; code was reverted and the repo returned to the v26 code state. v28 disables the dsp56k JIT optimizer by default for MD/MM and improved the headless MM spike-amplitude probe, but v30 records Thor's host A/B: MD got worse and MM was neutral. v31 restores optimizer-on as the plugin/default behavior and leaves GEARMULATOR_MDMM_JIT_OPTIMIZER=0 as the diagnostic opt-out path. v32 tests whether the safe UC batch cap can move above 16; evidence rejects it: 20 passes but is slower, 24 fails audio with silence. v33 keeps the mdLib link-ring candidate: it is bit-identical in local smoke/A-B, builds VST3, gives a small Windows/MSVC headless win and a small but host-positive DAW CPU result.
last_verified_host_result: Thor host A/B after v33 link-ring VST3 build: MM CPU ~82.5-83% (previous MM around ~84%); MD CPU ~72% (around PR97/v31 baseline). Thor accepted the change: keep the link-ring fix because it is bit-identical and slightly better in host. Earlier v29/v30 host A/B still rejects optimizer-default-off: PR97 MD ~71-72%, v28 MD ~75%, MM neutral ~84%.

current_measurements.linkring_candidate_v33: Applied Claude's mdLib-only link-ring candidate package linkring-candidate-on-85eb1f0d.patch, sha256 49d45477a8348b0ae1718f318b6b9d525f52363ad15a7b4549c2dc7fc53f6ea0. Patch changes mddsp.cpp/.h, mdhardware.cpp/.h, transportScorecardFirmwareTest.cpp and adds mdlinkring.h; no submodule/env/instrumentation. Root cause: DSP2<->DSP1 ESSI link used the 32768-frame ESSI audio input ring (~17 MB) as a one-word mailbox, walking cold cache/TLB lines; new LinkInputRing keeps FIFO semantics/capacity/prefill while storing only link words and rewinding when drained. Local Windows/MSVC headless verification: patch applies cleanly at top 85eb1f0d + DSP 6f8d1ce4, mmAudio base/candidate all PASS, MD audio filtered output identical, MD UW output differs only in benchmark timing line, VST3 build PASS. Thor host DAW A/B accepted keeping the fix: MM CPU ~82.5-83% vs previous ~84%, MD CPU ~72% circa.

active_hypotheses: Pure time-skip for the DSP2 CVR poll loop is unsafe: CVR reads must still invoke m_readCvrCallback so DSP catch-up and host-command acceptance timing remain real.

A full CVR loop accelerator is only viable if it batches taken iterations while still performing CVR reads and checking host-pump/deferred-RX/IRQ/timer/MIDI boundaries between MOVE and BLT. The single-MOVE fast path is rejected by measurement.

DSP2 heavier steady-state wall time is real work, but the large per-block spikes are now attributed to synchronous live DSP JIT compilation inside render callbacks; steady non-JIT windows still hover near the 5.805 ms budget and need separate DSP2 throughput work.

A simple first-PC/static-branch prewarm is insufficient: the trace shows dynamic/low-vector repeated compile events after boot. v23 classified the repeats: P-memory invalidation is not the main cause; the same PCs compile under multiple SR-mode JIT chains. v24 further shows naive hot-PC prewarm across existing chains regresses; a useful fix must avoid creating more wrong/soon-invalidated blocks and must target the actual live create path.

Cycle-counted interpreter fallback is now technically possible, but both attempted cold-create fallback hooks are rejected by evidence: unbounded one-step RT fallback reached INVALID PC ffdf8c, and queued post-callback compilation still reached INVALID PC ff0000 even with fallback budget 1. The issue is deeper than simply compiling queued blocks after the callback; the next attempt must preserve the JIT dispatcher/control-flow contract, not just replace create() with an interpreter step.

Disabling the JIT optimizer reduces synchronous cold compile spike amplitude in the headless MM probe, but Thor's host A/B disproves it as a default plugin policy: MD CPU regresses and MM is neutral. v31 therefore restores optimizer-on default; keep optimizer-off only as a diagnostic opt-out.
next_steps: If continuing UC work, prototype a full taken-iteration CVR loop batch with explicit post-CVR host boundary checks, not the rejected single-MOVE path.

If continuing DSP work, do not use simple boot-time hot-PC prewarm, unbounded one-step RT interpreter fallback, or the failed queued cold-create fallback hook. The cycle-counted primitive is proven, but the next viable direction must first trace the JIT dispatcher/control-flow contract around funcCreate() and prove a safe way to return after a counted interpreter step before trying another non-RT compile queue.
After JIT spikes are removed, target steady DSP2 throughput because dsp2 remains the largest total wall-time component (~149.55 ms/window vs uc ~113.18 ms and dsp1 ~98.34 ms in v21 profile).
Do not raise GEARMULATOR_MDMM_UC_BATCH default above 16: v32 shows 20 passes but is slower, 24 fails audio. Further UC work needs a new mechanism, not retuning this batch cap.
If continuing performance work after v33, investigate the nested DSP1 catch-up cost in the DSP2->DSP1 link path; keep bit-identical output as the acceptance gate.
Keep PR #98 separate from the v33 performance path: port/test it with repeated note-starts on MM tracks 4-6 before treating it as a correctness candidate.
